where $Y_{n(m)}$ denotes the value of $Y_{n}$ at the pole of $P_{m}$.
We may obtain the same result by the following shorter
process :-
Let a system of rectangular coordinates be taken so that the
axis of $z$ coincides with the axis of $P_{m}$, and let $Y_{n} r^{n}$ be expanded
as a homogeneous function of $x, y, z$ of degree $n$.
At the pole of $P_{m}, x=y=0$ and $z=r$, so that if $C z^{n}$ is the
term not involving $x$ or $y, C$ is the value of $Y_{n}$ at the pole of $Y_{i n}$.
Equation (31) becomes in this case
$$\iint Y_{n} P_{n} d s=\frac{4 \pi a^{2}}{2 n+1} \frac{1}{n!} \frac{d^{m}}{d z^{m}}\left(Y_{n} r^{n}\right)$$
As $m$ is equal to $n$, the result of differentiating $C z^{n}$ is $\|!C$, and

$$\iint Y_{n} P_{m} d s=\frac{4 \pi a^{2}}{2 n+1} C$$
$C$ being the value of $Y_{n}$ at the pole of $P_{m}$.

spherical harmonics, as it shews how to determine a series of
spherical harmonics which expresses the value of a quantity
